brief: My courtyard is full sun with low moisture, and one dog lives in the household. A hot, dry, sun-baked courtyard with a dog who digs and rubs against everything.

design.site_summary: A sunny, warm microclimate for a curious feline companion where safety and vibrant greenery take priority.
design.layout_strategy: Trailing plants cascade from the vertical railing at eye level, upright structural grasses and succulents anchor the mid-layer containers, and a low carpet of safe succulents occupies the ground layer along the balcony edge.
design.combination_logic: The combination relies on contrasting architectural forms and textures, pairing the fine fountain-like blades of Pampas Grass with the rosettes of Echeveria and Haworthia, alongside the delicate trailing habit of Alyssum. This mix provides year-round structural interest and seasonal flowering accents.

zones.placement: on the south-facing railing, receiving 5 hours of direct afternoon sun, fully exposed to gentle breezes.

plants.why: Provides a lush trailing habit suitable for hanging baskets and vertical display.
plants.role_in_combination: Adds soft texture and a continuous cascade of delicate flowers at eye level, contrasting with the stiff upright forms below.

maintenance: Water thoroughly when the top inch of soil feels dry.
Feed with a mild organic fertilizer monthly during spring and summer.

zones.placement: in a large ceramic pot against the warm interior wall, receiving 4 hours of bright morning sun and shelter from harsh winds.

plants.why: Serves as a striking architectural focal point with low water needs.
plants.role_in_combination: Provides strong vertical height and a dramatic fountain of cascading foliage that anchors the entire container grouping.

plants.why: Adds height, rustling texture, and feathery plumes.
plants.role_in_combination: Complements the Pony Tail palm with fine linear foliage and soft architectural plumes that sway in the breeze.

maintenance: Water deeply but infrequently, allowing the soil to dry out completely between waterings.
Prune back old dead leaves at the base in late winter.

zones.placement: on the accessible low wooden bench near the sliding door, receiving 3 hours of partial sun and easily reached by the cat.

plants.why: Forms tight, tactile rosettes that are completely pet-safe to brush against and nibble.
plants.role_in_combination: Creates a dense, geometric ground cover layer with fleshy blue-green leaves that contrast with the fine grasses.

plants.why: Provides interesting patterned foliage within paw's reach without any toxicity risks.
plants.role_in_combination: Adds dark green color and striking white tubercles for textural variation right at the front of the display.

maintenance: Water sparingly around the base every two weeks in summer, and monthly in winter.
Remove any dried lower leaves to maintain plant hygiene.

care_instructions.task: Water the succulent zones thoroughly and let soil dry out completely
care_instructions.frequency: every two weeks in summer, monthly in winter

care_instructions.task: Check moisture levels of the hanging Alyssum basket
care_instructions.frequency: twice a week in summer, weekly in spring and autumn

care_instructions.task: Inspect foliage for pests and clean dust off the leaves

care_cautions: Overwatering the Pony Tail and succulent containers can lead to root rot; ensure pots have adequate drainage holes.
The trailing Alyssum in the hanging basket may dry out faster during peak afternoon heatwaves on the south-facing railing.
design.pet_safety_note: Every plant selected (Alyssum, Pony Tail, Pampas Grass, Hens and Chickens, and Little Zebra Plant) is entirely non-toxic to cats and dogs, ensuring complete safety even if your pet decides to graze.
